rice_blast.causes: Caused by the fungus Magnaporthe oryzae. Spreads through airborne spores. Favoured by high humidity (>90%), temperatures 25-28°C, heavy nitrogen fertilization, and cloudy weather. Common in Odisha's Kharif season.
rice_blast.symptoms: Diamond-shaped grey lesions with brown margins on leaves. In severe cases, the neck of the panicle turns brown and breaks (neck blast), causing white empty panicles — a total yield loss situation.

mild.description: Few scattered lesions on lower leaves, less than 5% leaf area affected
mild.treatment: Remove and destroy infected leaves. Improve field drainage. Avoid excess urea. Apply wood ash around plants.
mild.frequency: Once at first sign, repeat after 10 days if needed
mild.spray_time: Early morning or evening, avoid midday
mild.organic_alternative: Spray 1kg fermented buttermilk + 1kg neem leaf extract in 10L water

moderate.description: Lesions on 5-25% leaf area, some neck infection visible
moderate.treatment: Immediate fungicide application. Drain excess water from field. Do not apply nitrogen fertilizer until disease is controlled.
moderate.dosage: 1.5 ml per liter of water (15ml in 10L)
moderate.organic_alternative: Pseudomonas fluorescens @ 2.5 kg/ha as soil drench + foliar spray

severe.description: More than 25% leaf area affected, widespread neck blast, panicle death
severe.treatment: Emergency chemical treatment. Spray within 24 hours. If neck blast is widespread, protect remaining panicles. Consider partial harvest of mature panicles.
severe.emergency_action: Alert the local KVK immediately. Document damage for crop insurance claim.

rice_blast.organic_alternative: Trichoderma viride 4g/kg seed treatment before sowing. Spray Pseudomonas fluorescens 0.5% WP at 2.5 kg/ha.
prevention_tips: Use blast-resistant varieties: Improved Samba Mahsuri, MTU 1010, Swarna Sub1
Seed treatment with Carbendazim 2g/kg before sowing
Balanced fertilization — do not over-apply urea
Maintain proper spacing for air circulation
Drain field when blast appears — drought stress reduces blast
rice_blast.ipm_notes: Source: ICAR-NRRI Cuttack (Odisha) blast management protocol 2023

rice_brown_spot.causes: Fungal disease worsened by potassium and silicon deficiency. Thrives in poor soils and waterlogged conditions. The 1943 Bengal Famine was partly caused by this disease — showing its devastating historical potential.
rice_brown_spot.symptoms: Oval to circular brown spots with a yellow halo on leaves and glumes. Spots have a light grey or white center. Infected seeds produce brown discolored grain (stackburn).

mild.description: A few spots on lower leaves, less than 5% infection
mild.treatment: Apply potash fertilizer (MOP) 20 kg/acre. Improve drainage. Spray neem oil solution.
mild.frequency: One spray, repeat if needed after 15 days
mild.organic_alternative: Spray 10% neem leaf extract or garlic-chili extract solution

moderate.description: Spots on 5-20% of leaf area, grain infection starting
moderate.treatment: Fungicide spray + potassium fertilization. Check soil pH and correct if needed.

severe.description: More than 20% leaf area, grain discoloration, yield loss certain
severe.treatment: Immediate chemical treatment. Apply silicon @ 25 kg/acre. Ensure proper drainage.
severe.emergency_action: Apply potash fertilizer immediately. Contact agriculture department.

rice_brown_spot.organic_alternative: Seed treatment with Trichoderma viride 4g/kg. Foliar spray of 3% wood ash extract.
prevention_tips: Use balanced NPK + potash fertilization
Use certified disease-free seeds
Seed treatment with fungicide before sowing
Maintain proper plant spacing
Improve soil health with organic compost
rice_brown_spot.ipm_notes: Source: NIPHM IPM guidelines for Kharif rice

rice_leaf_blight.causes: Bacterial disease spread by wind and rain splash. Enters through water pores (hydathodes) at leaf tips. Explosive spread after storms and cyclones — very relevant in coastal Odisha.
rice_leaf_blight.symptoms: Water-soaked lesions starting at leaf tips and margins, turning yellow then brown-grey. Leaves appear dried. Milky bacterial ooze visible in early morning (Kresek phase in seedlings = rapid wilting).

mild.description: Tip burning on few leaves, less than 10% plants affected
mild.treatment: Remove infected plant material. Avoid field operations when leaves are wet. Stop nitrogen application.
mild.organic_alternative: Spray 5% Panchagavya or copper sulfate solution 0.2%

moderate.treatment: Bactericide spray. Drain standing water. Apply potash to strengthen plant resistance.

severe.description: More than 30% plants affected, kresek phase visible in nursery/young crops
severe.treatment: Emergency bactericide treatment. Drain and reflood with fresh water. Do not apply nitrogen.
severe.emergency_action: Drain field. Stop all nitrogen fertilizer. File crop insurance claim if damage exceeds 33%.

rice_leaf_blight.organic_alternative: PGPR seed treatment. Spray BSO (Bacillus subtilis) biocontrol agent.
prevention_tips: Plant resistant varieties: IR64, Swarna, Tapaswini (Odisha)
Avoid excess urea — makes plants susceptible
Drain fields after heavy rain/cyclone
Seed treatment with Streptomycin 1g per liter for 12 hours
Do not transplant from infected nurseries
rice_leaf_blight.ipm_notes: Source: ICAR-NRRI Cuttack BLB management protocol

wheat_rust.causes: Highly contagious airborne fungal disease. Uredospores travel hundreds of kilometers on wind. The Ug99 strain is a global emergency threat. Favors temperatures 15-25°C with dew.
wheat_rust.symptoms: Orange-brown oval pustules (uredinia) on stems, leaves, and leaf sheaths. Pustules break open releasing rust-colored powder (spores). Black teliospores form later in season. Severely weakens stems causing lodging.

mild.description: Scattered pustules on lower leaves only, less than 5% infection
mild.treatment: Monitor closely. Apply protective fungicide. Remove severely infected plants.
mild.organic_alternative: Spray sulfur dust 20 kg/acre or potassium bicarbonate solution

moderate.description: Pustules on multiple leaves and some stems, 5-25% infection
moderate.treatment: Systemic fungicide immediately. Two rounds of treatment.

severe.description: Widespread stem infection, lodging risk, more than 25% affected
severe.treatment: Emergency systemic fungicide. Stems compromised — act immediately before lodging.
severe.emergency_action: Immediate harvest if crop is near maturity. Alert district agriculture officer.

wheat_rust.organic_alternative: Use rust-resistant varieties. Bioagent Trichoderma seed treatment.
prevention_tips: Plant rust-resistant varieties: GW 322, HD 2781, K 307
Timely sowing (November in North India)
Avoid excess nitrogen — lush growth favors rust
Monitor fields weekly from tillering stage
Remove volunteer wheat and barberry plants nearby
wheat_rust.ipm_notes: Source: ICAR-IIWBR Karnal wheat protection guidelines

wheat_powdery_mildew.causes: Obligate fungal parasite — can only grow on living wheat tissue. Spreads via airborne conidia. Favors cool temperatures (15-20°C) with high humidity. Dense crop canopy accelerates spread.
wheat_powdery_mildew.symptoms: White to grey powdery fungal growth (mycelium + conidia) on upper leaf surface. Affected leaves turn yellow and die. Primarily attacks upper leaves and spikes in severe cases.

mild.description: Powdery patches on lower leaves only
mild.treatment: Improve air circulation. Remove severely infected tillers. Sulfur-based fungicide.
mild.spray_time: Morning (avoid hot hours — sulfur can burn in heat)

moderate.description: Upper leaves affected, 5-20% of crop showing mildew
moderate.treatment: Systemic fungicide application. Remove excess tillers for better air circulation.
moderate.organic_alternative: Neem oil 3ml + mild soap 1ml per liter spray

severe.description: Flag leaf and spike infection, more than 20% crop affected
severe.treatment: Immediate systemic treatment. Flag leaf infection directly reduces grain fill.
severe.emergency_action: Treat flag leaf emergence as absolute priority. Document for insurance.

wheat_powdery_mildew.organic_alternative: Trichoderma seed treatment. Spray milk dilution (1:9 milk:water) as preventive.
prevention_tips: Plant resistant varieties: PBW 343, WH 1105, DBW 88
Avoid dense planting — maintain 20cm row spacing
Balanced fertilization — avoid excess nitrogen
Timely fungicide spray at first sign
Crop rotation to break disease cycle
wheat_powdery_mildew.ipm_notes: Source: ICAR wheat crop protection guidelines 2023

tomato_early_blight.causes: Soilborne fungus that survives in plant debris for years. Spreads through water splash. Favors warm temperatures (24-29°C) with alternating wet-dry cycles. Older leaves attacked first — classic pattern.
tomato_early_blight.symptoms: Dark brown to black circular spots with concentric rings (target board pattern) on older lower leaves. Yellow halo around spots. Spots on stem cause collar rot in seedlings.

mild.treatment: Remove infected lower leaves. Mulch soil to prevent splash. Stake plants for better air flow.
mild.organic_alternative: Spray compost tea or Bacillus subtilis solution

moderate.description: Multiple leaves infected, spots coalescing, 10-30% defoliation
moderate.treatment: Fungicide spray. Remove and destroy fallen leaves. Improve drainage.

severe.description: More than 30% defoliation, stem cankers, fruit infection
severe.treatment: Systemic + contact fungicide mix. Severe defoliation threatens photosynthesis and yield.
severe.emergency_action: Remove severely infected plants. Avoid overhead irrigation.

tomato_early_blight.organic_alternative: Spray 1% Bordeaux mixture (copper sulfate + lime). Trichoderma soil drench.
prevention_tips: Use resistant varieties: Arka Rakshak, Arka Samrat
Avoid overhead irrigation — use drip irrigation
Mulch with straw or plastic to prevent soil splash
Remove and destroy crop debris after harvest
2-3 year crop rotation with non-solanaceous crops
tomato_early_blight.ipm_notes: Source: ICAR-IIVR Varanasi tomato disease management

tomato_late_blight.causes: The pathogen that caused the Irish Potato Famine (1845-1849) — killing 1 million people. Not a true fungus but a water mold. Spreads explosively in cool, wet conditions. Can destroy a field in 3-5 days under favorable conditions.
tomato_late_blight.symptoms: Water-soaked, greasy spots on leaves and stems that turn brown-black rapidly. White fluffy mold (sporangia) visible on undersides of leaves in humid weather. Dark brown lesions on fruit surface extending into fruit flesh.

mild.description: First lesions appearing on lower leaves, less than 5% plants affected
mild.treatment: Remove infected leaves immediately. Avoid overhead irrigation. Apply preventive fungicide.
mild.spray_time: Morning — NEVER evening (spores spread at night)

moderate.description: Multiple plants infected, lesions on stems, 10-30% damage
moderate.treatment: Systemic fungicide immediately. Stop all overhead irrigation. Stake plants.

severe.description: More than 30% plants collapsing, field-wide spread, fruit rot
severe.treatment: Emergency. This disease is a RACE — act immediately or lose the crop.
severe.emergency_action: If fruit already infected — harvest whatever is healthy immediately. Consider emergency harvest.

tomato_late_blight.organic_alternative: Bordeaux mixture 1% (proven since 1800s). Copper oxychloride spray.
prevention_tips: Never plant in areas with history of late blight
Use certified disease-free seed/transplants
Avoid overhead irrigation — drip only
Ensure good spacing and air circulation
Apply preventive copper fungicide at transplanting
Scout field every 2-3 days during monsoon
tomato_late_blight.ipm_notes: Source: ICAR late blight emergency management protocol. HISTORICAL NOTE: P. infestans caused the Great Irish Famine.

tomato_leaf_curl.causes: Transmitted exclusively by whitefly (Bemisia tabaci). THERE IS NO CHEMICAL CURE FOR THE VIRUS — only whitefly control can prevent spread. Once a plant has the virus, it cannot be cured.
tomato_leaf_curl.symptoms: Leaves curl upward and inward, becoming thick and leathery. Interveinal yellowing. Stunted plant growth. Flowers may fall without setting fruit. Plants infected early produce no yield.

mild.description: 1-5 plants showing symptoms, whitefly population moderate
mild.treatment: Remove and destroy infected plants IMMEDIATELY to prevent spread. Control whitefly vector.
mild.pesticide_name: Imidacloprid 17.8% SL (Confidor / Tatamida) for whitefly control
mild.dosage: 0.3ml per liter (for whitefly — insecticide, not fungicide)
mild.frequency: Spray every 7 days for whitefly control
mild.spray_time: Evening (whiteflies active in morning — contact spray more effective in evening)
mild.organic_alternative: Yellow sticky traps 20/acre. Neem oil 5ml/L spray for whitefly.

moderate.treatment: Remove ALL infected plants. Intensive whitefly control. Consider border planting with maize as barrier.
moderate.organic_alternative: Beauveria bassiana biocontrol spray for whitefly

severe.description: More than 20% plants infected, epidemic spread
severe.treatment: Remove all infected plants. Apply reflective mulch to confuse whiteflies. Consider crop abandonment if more than 50% infected.
severe.pesticide_name: Spiromesifen 22.9% SC (Oberon) — targets whitefly eggs and nymphs
severe.emergency_action: IMPORTANT: No virus cure exists. Focus entirely on preventing whitefly from spreading to healthy plants.

tomato_leaf_curl.organic_alternative: Yellow sticky traps, reflective silver mulch, companion planting with basil. Neem cake soil application.
prevention_tips: Use TYLCV-resistant varieties: Arka Rakshak, Pusa Hybrid-1
Install 40-mesh nylon net in nursery to exclude whiteflies
Use silver reflective mulch — whiteflies avoid bright light
Plant border rows of maize or sorghum as wind barrier
Do not plant near fields with history of leaf curl
tomato_leaf_curl.ipm_notes: Source: ICAR-IIHR viral disease management. KEY: No cure, only prevention/vector control.

potato_late_blight.causes: Same devastating pathogen as tomato late blight. Particularly destructive in potato because tubers in soil also get infected. Cool (10-20°C), wet weather with high humidity causes explosive spread.
potato_late_blight.symptoms: Dark brown-black water-soaked lesions on leaves starting at margins. White mold on lower leaf surface. Brown rotting of tubers in soil — undetectable until harvest.

mild.description: First lesions on lower leaves, 3-5 plants in a patch
mild.treatment: Remove infected haulms. Apply preventive fungicide immediately. Reduce irrigation.

moderate.description: Patches of infected plants, 10-25% foliage affected
moderate.treatment: Systemic fungicide. Kill and bury haulms of infected plants to prevent tuber spread.

severe.description: Field-wide infection, haulm collapse, tuber rot in soil
severe.treatment: Emergency. Kill haulms by cutting/herbicide to stop infection moving to tubers. Harvest early.
severe.emergency_action: Destroy haulms immediately. Delay harvest 2-3 weeks after killing haulms for skin set. Check tubers carefully before storing.

potato_late_blight.organic_alternative: Bordeaux mixture. Copper sulfate spray. Biocontrol Bacillus subtilis.
prevention_tips: Plant certified disease-free seed potato
Avoid planting in low-lying areas
Earthing-up protects tubers from spores
Use late blight resistant varieties: Kufri Jyoti, Kufri Bahar
Destroy volunteer potato plants and nightshade weeds
potato_late_blight.ipm_notes: Source: ICAR-CPRI Shimla potato disease management guidelines

potato_black_scurf.causes: Soilborne fungus that persists in soil for many years. Infected seed tubers are the main source. Cool, wet soils slow emergence and increase infection window.
potato_black_scurf.symptoms: Black or brown crusty sclerotia (fungal resting structures) on tuber surface — like dirt that won't wash off. Stem canker causes girdling of underground stems, yellowing and purple-red discoloration of above-ground leaves.

mild.description: Black spots on tuber skin only, no stem canker, plants growing normally
mild.treatment: No in-season chemical treatment changes much. Tubers are marketable if consumers accept. Focus on seed treatment for next crop.
mild.dosage: 3g per kg of seed tubers (for next crop)
mild.organic_alternative: Trichoderma viride seed treatment 10g per kg

moderate.description: Stem canker visible, some plant stunting, 10-25% plants affected
moderate.treatment: Soil drench around affected plants. Improve drainage.
moderate.dosage: 1g per liter, drench around plant base
moderate.frequency: One treatment at stem canker appearance
moderate.organic_alternative: Trichoderma harzianum soil drench 2.5 kg/ha in 500L water

severe.description: Widespread stem canker, plant wilting, significant yield loss
severe.treatment: Limited in-season options. Improve drainage. Apply gypsum to improve soil. Focus on harvest and next season.
severe.dosage: Per label, applied at planting in next season
severe.emergency_action: Harvest as soon as possible. Sort and store only clean tubers. Do not save infected seed for next crop.

potato_black_scurf.organic_alternative: Trichoderma seed treatment. Well-decomposed organic matter improves soil biology to suppress Rhizoctonia.
prevention_tips: Use certified disease-free seed tubers
Treat seed with Carbendazim before cutting
Plant in well-drained soils
Avoid planting in same field repeatedly
Incorporate organic matter to promote beneficial microbes

maize_leaf_spot.causes: Fungal disease spreading through air and water. Favors moderate temperatures (18-27°C) with frequent dew and rain. Older leaves infected first, moving upward.
maize_leaf_spot.symptoms: Long, elliptical (cigar-shaped) gray-green to tan lesions, 2.5-15cm long, following the leaf veins. Multiple lesions coalesce causing large dead areas. Severe infection before tasseling drastically reduces yield.

mild.description: Lesions on lower leaves only, less than 10% leaf area
mild.treatment: Remove infected leaves if accessible. Apply protective fungicide.

moderate.description: Mid-canopy leaves infected, 10-30% leaf area, approaching tasseling
moderate.treatment: Systemic fungicide. Timing is critical — protect leaves above the ear.

severe.description: Upper leaf canopy infected before/during tasseling, ear leaves affected, more than 30%
severe.treatment: Immediate systemic fungicide to save ear leaf and flag leaf — crucial for grain fill.
severe.emergency_action: Focus on protecting ear leaf and two leaves above/below ear. These 3 leaves are responsible for most grain fill.

maize_leaf_spot.organic_alternative: Bioagent Trichoderma seed treatment. Pseudomonas fluorescens foliar spray.
prevention_tips: Plant resistant hybrids: DKC 9108, Bio 9681, Pioneer P3396
Rotate with non-grass crops (legumes, vegetables)
Balanced NPK fertilization
Avoid overhead irrigation
Maintain proper plant density
maize_leaf_spot.ipm_notes: Source: ICAR-IIMR (Indian Institute of Maize Research) disease management

maize_rust.causes: Airborne rust fungus. Spreads extremely fast under cool, humid conditions (16-23°C). New crops can be infected from spores traveling long distances. Sorrel (Oxalis) is an alternate host — removing it helps.
maize_rust.symptoms: Small, circular to elongate, brick-red to brown powdery pustules (uredia) on both leaf surfaces. Unlike leaf blight (which has elongated lesions), rust pustules are small and round. Leaves may yellow and die with severe infection.

mild.description: Scattered small pustules on lower leaves, less than 5% leaf area
mild.treatment: Monitor crop. Protective spray if conditions favor spread.

moderate.description: Pustules on multiple leaves, 5-20% infection, spreading upward

severe.description: Widespread pustules on upper canopy, flag leaf and ear leaves affected
severe.treatment: Emergency systemic fungicide. Severe rust can reduce yield 30-50%.
severe.emergency_action: Protect ear leaf region. If near maturity, consider early harvest.

maize_rust.organic_alternative: Wettable sulfur spray. Biological control with Trichoderma.
prevention_tips: Plant rust-resistant hybrids
Early planting avoids peak rust pressure
Remove Oxalis (sorrel) weeds from and around field
Balanced potassium fertilization strengthens cell walls
maize_rust.ipm_notes: Source: ICAR-IIMR maize disease management guidelines

cotton_bollworm.causes: Major polyphagous insect pest — attacks 181+ plant species. Female moth lays eggs on young leaves; larvae bore into bolls, buds and flowers. Most devastating when it attacks bolls (cotton seed capsules).
cotton_bollworm.symptoms: Circular entry holes in bolls/flower buds. Larva (caterpillar) visible inside boll. Bolls shed prematurely. Internal boll damage with frass (insect excrement) visible. Damaged squares (flower buds) drop.

mild.description: Less than 5% boll damage, few larvae visible
mild.treatment: Hand pick and destroy larvae. Install pheromone traps for monitoring.
mild.pesticide_name: Spinosad 45% SC (Tracer) or Emamectin Benzoate 5% SG (Proclaim)
mild.frequency: One spray, monitor with pheromone traps
mild.spray_time: Evening (larvae active at night, better contact)
mild.organic_alternative: Bt (Bacillus thuringiensis) spray 2g/L. Nuclear Polyhedrosis Virus (NPV) of Helicoverpa 250 LE/ha.

moderate.description: 5-20% boll damage, multiple larvae per plant
moderate.treatment: Spray systemic insecticide. Pheromone traps 5/acre. Remove and destroy damaged bolls.
moderate.organic_alternative: NPV-H 250 LE/ha spray. Trichogramma egg parasitoid release.

severe.description: More than 20% boll damage, economic threshold exceeded, 2+ larvae per plant
severe.treatment: Emergency systemic insecticide rotation (important: rotate to prevent resistance).
severe.emergency_action: RESISTANCE MANAGEMENT: Never use same insecticide class twice in a row. Helicoverpa has developed resistance to many chemicals. Rotate modes of action.

cotton_bollworm.organic_alternative: Bt var. kurstaki spray. NPV of Helicoverpa. Trichogramma chilonis parasitoid release.
prevention_tips: Use Bt cotton varieties (provides built-in resistance)
Install 5 pheromone traps per acre for early monitoring
Intercrop with trap crops (marigold, pigeonpea)
Deep ploughing after harvest destroys pupae in soil
Avoid continuous cotton — rotate with wheat/sorghum
cotton_bollworm.ipm_notes: Source: CICR (Central Institute for Cotton Research) Nagpur IPM guidelines

cotton_leaf_curl.causes: Devastating viral disease transmitted by whitefly Bemisia tabaci. Has devastated Punjab and Haryana cotton in 1990s (30 lakh acres affected). New strains continuously overcome resistant varieties.
cotton_leaf_curl.symptoms: Leaves curl downward (unlike tomato leaf curl which curls upward). Enations (leaf-like outgrowths) on underside of leaves — DIAGNOSTIC feature. Thickened, dark green veins. Severe stunting. No yield if infected early.

mild.description: 1-5% plants showing symptoms, whitefly population low
mild.treatment: Uproot and destroy infected plants. Control whitefly immediately.
mild.organic_alternative: Yellow sticky traps 10/acre. Neem oil 5ml/L for whitefly.

moderate.treatment: Rogue out all infected plants. Intensive whitefly management. Add border crops.
moderate.organic_alternative: Beauveria bassiana spray for whitefly biocontrol

severe.treatment: VIRUS CANNOT BE CURED. Focus entirely on whitefly elimination to save uninfected plants.
severe.emergency_action: Remove all infected plants from field. Consider abandoning severely affected crop. File insurance claim.

cotton_leaf_curl.organic_alternative: Reflective mulch. Marigold border planting. Neem cake soil application reduces whitefly.
prevention_tips: Plant CLCuD-resistant varieties: RCH 134 Bt, MRC 7301 Bt
Avoid late planting (high whitefly pressure in late season)
Install yellow sticky traps before crop establishes
Avoid planting near tomato, brinjal (alternate hosts for whitefly)
Do not save seed from infected crop
cotton_leaf_curl.ipm_notes: Source: CICR cotton virus disease management. NOTE: No chemical cure for virus — vector control is everything.

healthy_leaf.causes: No disease detected. Plant appears healthy.
healthy_leaf.symptoms: Normal leaf color (green), no spots, no discoloration, normal leaf shape and texture.

mild.treatment: No treatment needed. Continue regular care.
mild.organic_alternative: Preventive organic spray: neem oil monthly

moderate.organic_alternative: Maintain balanced nutrition with organic compost

healthy_leaf.organic_alternative: Preventive care: neem cake application, regular monitoring.
prevention_tips: Continue regular monitoring for early disease detection
Maintain proper irrigation and drainage
Apply balanced fertilizers as per soil test
Keep field clean of weeds and crop debris
Monitor for insects and apply IPM practices
healthy_leaf.ipm_notes: No disease detected. The model is confident the plant is healthy.
